thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: KV cache prefix surge observed across multiple shards. continuous_batch queue length > 12k, total KV size ~3x baseline. Error spike on /v1/generate (502/504). Pager routed to oncall: sara
sara: i'm on it. seeing p90/p99 kv lookup latencies spike, lots of duplicate prefixes. could be prefetch amplification or a contbatch regression. @anjali can you pull shard heatmap and top prefixes?
anjali: pulling now. early look: shard s-47 and s-52 are hot. keys/shard s-47 ~1.8M (normal ~120k), s-52 ~1.5M. continuous_batch backlog shows long-lived chains stuck on MQA queries with huge prefix lengths. grabbing logs -> attaching snippets below.
anjali: ```
[08:09:42] runtime: contbatch_enqueue id=0x7f8 prefix_len=1024 user_query_type=MQA model=mistral-v1.2
[08:10:01] kv: lookup latency=1200ms key=pref:abcd... count=18432
[08:10:12] scheduler: contbatch_window_open id=0x7f8 window_size=4096
[08:10:18] runtime: memory pressure triggered eviction_delay=0
```
david: that log matches what i've seen in perf traces. MQA long-prefix patterns + aggressive prefetch are creating a miss storm and preventing timely eviction. continuous batching kernel keeps large KV windows which amplifies memory and I/O. immediate mitigation options: 1) reduce contbatch max_window to 64, 2) enable aggressive kv_prefetch_eviction, 3) route high-prefix-length requests to GQA-compatible fallback model (reduces MQA load). i'll prepare the config change.
mike: i can push the config change. plan: canary 10% -> monitor 2m -> full rollout if stable. command i'm going to run: ```
rctl apply -f - <<EOF
kind: ContBatchConfig
spec:
  max_window: 64
  backlog_threshold: 2000
  kv_prefetch_eviction: aggressive
EOF
```
opsbot: Deploy started: canary 10% -> 10 nodes. Monitoring metrics: /infra/metrics/kvcache/evictions, /runtime/p99, /runtime/error_rate. Posting updates to thread.
sara: support-ops, any active customer reports? think we should alert top affected customers and provide ETA.
support-ops: flagged 3 customers so far: AcmeCorp (realtime chat) seeing 10-20% 503s since 08:11 UTC; BetaApp intermittent latency spikes; PartnerX (ingest) elevated tail latency. sent AcmeCorp a brief note: "we're investigating increased error rates, mitigation in progress". no billing/regression notices yet.
opsbot: Canary stable after 90s. p99 on canary nodes dropped from ~1.8s -> ~350ms; error rate down to baseline. proceeding to full rollout.
mike: full rollout completed at 08:22 UTC. background eviction rate spiked during rollout then returned to normal. KV size now trending down from peak.
david: confirm: continuous batch queue length dropped from ~12k -> ~300. Mistral sigtail normalized. Qwen shows slight tail still ~2x baseline for top-percentile; i'll add routing rule to divert top 2% longest prefix requests to qwen-gqa-compat until we patch prefetch heuristics.
sara: putting this in incident mode. handoff note: next oncall @jordan starts 09:00 UTC; jordan please ack and pick up post-incident follow-up. action items for postmortem below.
jordan: ack. i'll take it and own the postmortem.
sara: immediate incident summary for postmortem: trigger = prefix cardinality blowup driven by MQA long-prefix queries combined with aggressive prefetch heuristics; amplification due to contbatch kernel holding large windows and delayed evictions. immediate mitigations = lowered contbatch max_window, turned on aggressive eviction for prefetch, fallback routing for heavy prefixes. next steps: add guardrails in prefetch (limit prefix cardinality), autoscale eviction threads under memory pressure, add new canary alarms for kv growth and contbatch queue length, and create synthetic evals for MQA long-prefix patterns. assign owners and deadlines.
anjali: I'll capture detailed metric snapshots, heatmaps, and top-key dumps and attach to the postmortem doc (will include sample logs and shard maps).
support-ops: customer communications sent: AcmeCorp updated at 08:25 UTC, BetaApp notified. customers acknowledged and waiting for postmortem.
sara: handing off live ownership to @jordan. marking mitigation complete and monitoring in watch mode for next 2 hours. if anything regresses, re-open pager. anyone else? :thumbsup: 
jordan: will create postmortem ticket and assign the items. thanks team.
incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. live mitigation actions applied: contbatch window reduced, kv_prefetch_eviction=aggressive, routing fallback enabled. resolving pager until monitoring period ends.
